body:
"Notice the masochistic tendency of leftist tactics. Leftists protest by
lying down in front of vehicles, they intentionally provoke police or
racists to abuse them, etc. These tactics may often be effective, but many
leftists use them not as a means to an end but because they PREFER
masochistic tactics. Self-hatred is a leftist trait." (Paragraph 20)

A while back I made a post about Stephen Donaldson, the founder of Stop
Prisoner Rape, and described his experience behind bars after being arrested
for protesting the Vietnam War.  Well, the ACLU, left wing activists, and
friends of his have made him into a hero.  Well, I think he was a punk --
and nothing more than that.

I think the heroes were those brave soldiers who fought and died for our
country.  I certainly didn't agree with the war, didn't agree with some of
our tactics, but damn it, those kids didn't want to be there; they risked
their lives for our country.  Yes, the puppet government we supported in
South Vietnam was corrupt, and communist sympathy there was pervasive.  But
look at what happened as soon as we deserted the effort: 8 million South
Vietnamese fled into exile and 200,000 died in the seas, wanting to escape
Communist oppression.

The average age of our troops was 19; these were kids!  At one point 100
were dying a day.  What was Jane Fonda doing?  Sitting on her fat leftist
arse reaping the rewards of capitalism and waving a Viet Cong flag while
they were fighting and dying.  Bitches like her make me sick; I WANT HER TO
FUCKING DIE.  I saw the public broadcasting special "Dear America: Letters
from Vietnam" and was deeply inspired, I felt pride in our country, right or
wrong I admired to valor of the soldiers.  And I wasn't even born yet during
the war.

To think of those cowardly reprobates, being priveleged college kids who
evaded the draft, spitting on our soldiers (many of whom were black and
hispanic) upon their return makes me sick.

Stephen Donaldson was not a hero, he was a punk.  A weak suburban white
punk.

It was easy for him to protest a war, but would he have been willing to
fight and die for anything?  Well, one thing I know for sure, he wasn't
willing to fight for his manhood while he was incarcerated.  He was
repeatedly raped behind bars, unwilling or unable to at least ATTEMPT to
defend himself.  Moreover, while he was getting violated he felt that he was
paying for the sins of society; he felt he deserved it!

Here he shows his self-hate and mental weakness:

"There were times when I felt like I was paying for all the sins of the
white race."

Here he describes the racially seething atmosphere in prison:

"Some guys were really, ah, were really rough, and they'd make racial
comments, for example, 'Your ass belongs to the black man. Don't you ever
forget it.'  Stuff like that, you know."

I think there are many more Steven Donaldson's in our society; Ted Kaczynski
described it as a disease.  TK took a major detour in the beginning of the
Manifesto just to talk about it.  These types are sheep; they will rarely,
if ever, challenge any fundamental beliefs of society but will latch onto
already accepted beliefs and gripe about people not following them enough.
They will do this under ANY system because they not only blithely follow the
the status quo, but worse, they are oversocialized COWARDS.

Being politically correct is NOT REBELLIOUS; it is conformity.  It is
fighting to preserve and enforce values which are already ingrained in our
society.
